newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dollar closes the year higher versus yen in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar closes the year higher versus yen in Asia.

text.p: 0745 GMT 0430 GMT NYK CLOSE

The dollar finished Asian trade for 1996 nudging its year high against the yen, dealers said on Tuesday. But the U.S. currency was a touch lower against the mark in very quiet trading on New Year's eve.
The dollar was well-bid throughout the day although light profit-taking dragged the currency down from an early high of 116.28 yen.
The dollar ended above 116 yen in New York overnight for the first time in 45 months.

"Sentiment is bullish and the dollar trend is heading upwards, but it lacks momentum to rise further today in the absence of Japanese traders and ahead of the New Year holiday," a dealer at a European bank in Hong Kong said.
He said the market was testing the patience of central banks to see when they stepped in to check the dollar's rise.
"The BOJ moves in to buy when the dollar falls but it seems unlikely that it would come in to sell to stem the rise unless the dollar touches the 120 yen level," he added.
Singapore dealers said the dollar was driven higher mostly by U.S. funds on speculation it would firm on favourable U.S. economic data, mainly the November index of leading indicators.
"U.S. overnight economic data, like leading indicators, was not bad, which helped the market rise with the bullish tide," a trader with a Singapore bank said.
Dollar/yen strength stirred demand today for other strong majors like sterling, which has risen against the yen to 169.0 yen, they added.
Investment and hedge funds were in favour of holding U.S. dollar on the face of positive interest rate differential.
"It is also highly likely that the U.S. will lift interest rates in the first quarter next year," a U.S. bank dealer in Hong Kong said.
Most traders expected the dollar to open higher in 1997, and with government officials quiet on the latest dollar rally, so participants tended to hold long positions, one dealer said.
The dollar saw no immediate resistance after it breached the 115 yen level and dealers forecast the unit to test 117-117.50 yen early next year.
"But the rise on dollar/mark is likely to be slowed by positive mark/yen cross," the U.S. bank dealer said.
The mark/yen was noted to be heavily long with buying also spurred by the weak yen position, Singapore dealers said. But profit taking looked like capping the rate at 74.80/90 in the short-term.
The dollar/mark was flat and tracking the dollar/yen, and the market was seen suspended between stop-buying at 1.5520 and 1.5555 stop-selling, they said.
Rumours that Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's health had deteroriated and that he was sent to hospital was also seen positive for the dollar/yen, a Hong Kong dealer said.
Dealers expected the dollar to remain quiet in Europe with ranges seen at 116.30-115.90 yen and 1.5550-1.5510 mark.
-- Alison Leung, Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6369
